issues.legal_issue: An arbitral award allocating partnership assets, including immovable property, among partners on dissolution requires compulsory registration only if it effects a transfer, partition, or extinguishment of rights in immovable property rather than distributing the residue after settlement of accounts.
material_facts: Partners in two firms referred their disputes to arbitration, and the award dissolved the firms and allocated properties to the partners.
The award dealt with properties belonging to the firms, including immovable properties, and allocated them as part of the distribution of the surplus after settlement of accounts.
The award did not purport to distribute the partners’ personal properties that the arbitrators had not found to belong to the firms.
The award had not been registered, and the High Court Division Bench held that registration was required before it could be made a rule of court.
issues.conclusion: The award distributed the residue of the dissolved firms after settlement of accounts and did not require compulsory registration; the contrary order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 14 and 48 of the Partnership Act, 1932, property brought into or acquired for a firm is firm property, and on dissolution the partners are entitled to their shares in the residue after accounts are settled. A partner has an undefined, fluctuating interest in the firm’s assets, not an earmarked interest in particular assets. Allocating firm property as part of the distribution of the residue is a mutual adjustment of the partners’ rights, not a partition, transfer, or extinguishment of an interest in immovable property under section 17(1) of the Registration Act, 1908. The Court relied on Addanki Narayanappa v. Bhaskara Krishtappa, Commissioner of Income Tax v. Juggilal Kamalapat, CIT v. Dewas Cine Corporation, CIT v. Bankey Lal Vaidya, and Malabar Fisheries Co. v. CIT; it distinguished Ratan Lal Sharma v. Purshottam Harit and Lachman Das v. Ram Lal, and referred to Ajudhia Pershad Ram Pershad v. Sham Sunder.

rule.if: arbitration_award_on_partnership_dissolution and firm_accounts_settled_before_distribution and award_distributes_firm_residue and firm_assets_include_immovable_property and not award_independently_transfers_or_partitions_property

predicates.arbitration_award_on_partnership_dissolu: Partners referred their disputes to arbitration, and the award dealt with dissolution of their partnership.
predicates.firm_accounts_settled_before_distributio: The award provided for settlement of the firm’s accounts before distribution among the partners.
predicates.award_distributes_firm_residue: The award allocated the surplus remaining from firm property to the partners.
predicates.firm_assets_include_immovable_property: The assets treated as belonging to the firm included immovable property.
predicates.award_independently_transfers_or_partiti: The award independently effected a transfer or partition of property rather than allocating firm assets as part of distributing the residue.

issues.definition: When an arbitration award on partnership dissolution allocates firm residue after accounts are settled, even where firm assets include immovable property, and does not independently transfer or partition property, the award is not compulsorily registrable.

issues.legal_issue: A partner’s objection, by itself, does not prevent registration of an award that has been presented for registration.
material_facts: The surviving arbitrators presented the award for registration.
A partner objected to registration, and the award remained pending with the registering authority.
The Supreme Court addressed the pending registration and the partner’s objection.
issues.conclusion: The award may be registered notwithstanding the partner’s objection if that objection is the only reason registration is being withheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Court expressly directed that the pending award may be registered despite a partner’s objection where that objection is the only reason for withholding registration.

predicates.pending_award_registration_proceeding: A proceeding concerning registration of an arbitral award is pending before the registering authority.
predicates.award_presented_for_registration: The surviving arbitrators presented the award to the registering authority for registration.
predicates.partner_objection_is_only_bar: A partner’s objection is the only reason the registering authority is withholding registration.

issues.definition: When an award has been presented for registration and a partner’s objection is the only bar in a pending registration proceeding, the registering authority may register the award.
